contents.bytes:
Tectonic Summary

The April 24, 2023, M 7.1 off the western coast of the island of Sumatra in Indonesia likely occurred as the result of shallow thrust faulting along the subduction zone interface between the Australia and Sunda plates. The earthquake occurred at a shallow depth of 15 km. Moment tensor solutions indicate slip occurred on a near-vertical fault striking to the northwest, or a shallowly dipping fault striking the northeast. The location, depth, and moment tensor are consistent with the earthquake being an intraplate earthquake rupturing along the plate boundary on the shallowly dipping fault indicated in the moment-tensor solutions. At the location of this earthquake, the Australian plate is moving north-northeast relative to the Sunda plate at a rate of approximately 73 mm/yr.

While commonly plotted as points on maps, earthquakes of this size are more appropriately described as slip over a larger fault area. Reverse events of the size of the April 24 earthquake are typically about 42 km long x 25 km wide (fault length x fault width).

The plate boundary region between the Australia and Sunda plates is highly seismically active, with past strong earthquakes having occurred within each of the Australia and Sunda plates as well as on the plate interface. Seven earthquakes above M 7.0 have occurred within 250 km of this event within the past century, a M 7.6 event in 2009 ~100k to the east of this April 24 event. This April 24, 2023, earthquake occurred ~325 km south-southwest of the 2005 M8.6 northern Sumatra earthquake which resulted in at least 1,000 fatalities.

One house destroyed in Kabupaten Tapanuli Selatan, one damaged in Kabupaten Nias Selatan and one damaged on Siberut. Power outages occurred in Sumatera Barat and Sumatera Utara. A tsunami with a wave height of 10 cm was recorded on Pulau Tanahbala.
